---
title: "Local rules and specialist help"
---

Use this handbook to prepare your thinking and your next conversation. Your university or another responsible body still has to make some decisions. This page lists those cases once, so the same warning does not interrupt every chapter.

## Who decides what?

| Your question | Where the answer comes from |
|---|---|
| What are my candidature deadlines, leave options, examination rules or complaint routes? | Your university's current graduate research rules and the office responsible for them. |
| Can this study, amendment, recruitment plan or data access proceed? | The relevant ethics, governance, safety, site, community or data authority. |
| Does this design, sample, measure or analysis suit my research question? | The relevant research literature and a supervisor, methodologist or other qualified specialist who understands the study. |
| May I store, link, share or dispose of these data? | The data owner or custodian and the current privacy, security, consent, ethics, contractual and institutional rules. |
| May I use this software or AI tool with research material? | The tool's current terms and the rules set by your institution, project agreements, ethics approval, funder and intended publisher. |
| Who qualifies as an author, and may this material be published or placed in a repository? | The authorship standard, author group, contracts, copyright owner, journal, funder, partner and university rules that apply to the output. |
| What must remain accessible when the project ends? | The institution, record owner, data custodian, funder, community or partner responsible for retention, disposal and handover. |

Keep a copy or note the date when the answer affects an approval, submission, right, safety measure or irreversible step. Rules and software change. A link that was correct last year may not be enough for a decision today.

## When someone may be harmed

Use emergency services for immediate danger. For serious distress, participant harm, bullying, harassment, discrimination, suspected misconduct, a privacy or security breach, or pressure to work outside an approval, contact the relevant confidential service rather than trying to investigate or resolve the case through the handbook.

Keep names, private correspondence, identifiable information and case details out of the public GitHub form. You can still suggest a general improvement without describing the people involved.

Use the handbook to prepare the question and gather the records. Take both to the person who can decide.
